subject: Dedicated GPU Pool: sizing, commit tiers, and throughput SLAs
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@fluvio.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Ruiz <carlos.ruiz@fluvio.ai>
Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity — baseline traffic + SLA questions

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're close to an executive decision about moving from a mixed-hosted approach to a Dedicated GPU pool for inference. Before we get legal and procurement engaged we need a concrete sizing proposal and an idea of how you price the commit tiers + any standard discounts. A couple of constraints from our side:  

- Typical steady-state: ~2,400 requests/min (40 req/s) for the bulk of the day; peaks up to ~7,200 req/min (120 req/s) during marketing bursts (10–15 minutes).
- Average request payload: 350 tokens in prompt; expected completion ~180 tokens (~530 tokens total).
- Concurrency model: many short-lived requests (conversational UI) with ~2.5 concurrent requests per active user; at peak we estimate ~1,500 concurrent requests.
- SLA ask: 95th pctl response latency under 400ms for the core interactive routes.

Attached is a small sample of production traffic from the last 30 days so you can look at token distributions and arrival patterns.

Questions we need answered in the proposal:
1) Suggested GPU pool size (instance types / #GPUs) for steady-state and for peak tolerance (with burst buffer/burst capacity).
2) Pricing for monthly reserved commits at 6/12/24 month terms and what discount bands look like.
3) A clear throughput guarantee (how you define it and how you measure it) and what happens when we exceed commit.
4) Any recommended operational knobs (batching windows, prefix caching) we should enable to meet the SLA without overspending.

Thanks — if easier, we can schedule a 30-min call to walk through numbers; Carlos and I are available Mon/Tue morning PT.

Best,
Elena
Elena Park
Head of ML Platform, Fluvio Analytics

Elena —

Appreciate the sample traffic and the clear constraints. I've looped in Ben (pricing) and will pull Marcus from infra sizing for a short calc. High-level notes up front:  

- We can meet the 95th pctl <400ms target for the interactive routes with a configuration that combines a 24/7 reserved pool sized for steady-state plus short-term burst capacity (pre-warmed GPUs or scheduled autoscale).
- We generally price Dedicated as a reserved GPU commit (monthly CPU/GPU equivalent hours) with incremental overage rates and explicit burst credits for short peaks. Discount bands depend on term length and committed GPU-hours.

I asked Marcus to run a conservative throughput model for two candidate instance types (A100 40GB and H100 80GB) using your token/profile; he'll post numbers in a follow-up so we can include an explicit #GPUs recommendation. Ben will propose 6/12/24 mo pricing bands once we pick the baseline pool.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity — baseline traffic + SLA questions

Thanks for the sample, Elena — good signal. I ran a quick sizing model with conservative latencies (model family similar to an Llama-2-ish encoder-decoder running mixed precision). Caveats: exact numbers depend on model reshape, quantization, and runtime kernels but these are practical starting points.

Assumptions:
- Model: medium-sized chat model, average decode length 180 tokens, prompt 350 tokens (total sequence length 530).
- Batch-friendly traffic (we can batch similar-length requests to raise throughput).
- Measured per-GPU throughput (conservative):
  - A100 40GB: ~45 requests/sec (p50 latency ~120ms, p95 ~380ms under steady batching)
  - H100 80GB: ~80 requests/sec (p50 ~85ms, p95 ~260ms)

Sizing math (steady-state 40 req/s):
- A100 path: 40 req/s ÷ 45 req/s ≈ 0.9 GPUs → 1 GPU for steady-state headroom.
- H100 path: 40 ÷ 80 ≈ 0.5 → 1 GPU as well.

Peak brief bursts (120 req/s sustained for 15 minutes):
- A100: 120 ÷ 45 ≈ 2.7 → round up to 3 GPUs to absorb peak without queuing.
- H100: 120 ÷ 80 = 1.5 → 2 GPUs.

Recommendation (operationally practical):
- Baseline reserved pool: 1 GPU (A100 or H100) sized for steady-state.
- Buffer for peak: reserve + burst credits that allow scheduled pre-warming to add 1–2 GPUs during marketing spikes (2–3 GPUs total during bursts).
- Autoscale policy: cold-start latencies can exceed SLA, so use pre-warm window of 10–15 minutes for larger scale-ups. For predictable 10–15 min bursts we recommend burst credits (no cold boot) or scheduled autoscale triggers.

Notes on latency/guarantee: the p95 numbers above assume queueing is avoided (sized GPU pool + batching). If you prefer a strict p95 SLA for all peaks, you'd size the pool to handle peak sustained RPS (A100: 3 GPUs; H100: 2 GPUs). That increases commit cost but removes reliance on burst credits.

I'll attach a quick worksheet with the per-GPU throughput curves and toggles for different token lengths.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

Elena — following Marcus's sizing, here's how we typically structure commit options and associated discounts:  

Pricing summary (list prices are illustrative; final quote will be on official paper):
- Monthly list rate (pay-as-you-go equivalent): $TBD per GPU-hour (baseline public rate).
- 6-month commit: ~7% discount off list on committed GPU-hours.
- 12-month commit: ~14% discount.
- 24-month commit: ~22% discount + additional operational credits (e.g., 5% burst credits included).

Commit shapes we recommend for your profile: 
- Conservative (cost-first): reserve 1 GPU 24/7 + 200 burst GPU-hours/month (covers several 15-min spikes). Good for teams that can tolerate scheduled pre-warms.
- Performance-first (SLA-strict): reserve 3 GPUs 24/7 (A100 path) or 2 GPUs 24/7 (H100 path) — no burst reliance; straightforward SLA mapping.

Overage and burst handling:
- Overage: meter usage over committed GPU-hours and bill at a clearly stated overage rate (typically list*1.15).
- Burst credits: for short windows we can include a bucket of burst GPU-hours (consumed before overage). Bursts do not count against 95th pctl SLA if they are served from pre-warmed/burst credits.

Next steps if you want a clean procurement package: we can propose 2 line items on the PO — the committed monthly GPU-hours (with term and discount) and a burst-credit bucket (monthly). I can draft sample numbers once we select A100 vs H100 and term length.

—Ben

Thanks all — helpful write-up. Two follow-ups from procurement and infra:  

1) Procurement: they're looking at a 12-month commit but want a safety valve — if we commit 12 months to the conservative plan (1 GPU + 200 burst hours) can we include a one-time upsize option after 90 days to move to the performance-first tier at a pro-rated rate (we'll pay the delta for the remainder of the term)?
2) Infra: H100s are preferred for latency; budget permitting we'd prefer the H100 path. Can you give an example monthly cost comparison (1x H100 + burst credits vs 2x H100 steady) and the break-even point where dedicating extra GPU 24/7 becomes cheaper than frequent burst-hour consumption?

If you can add a short table to the proposal showing 12-month cost for the conservative vs performance path (H100), that will speed procurement.

—Elena
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>

Elena —

All good asks. Ben and I talked and we can do the following for a 12-month commitment: 

- Contract terms: 12-month commit on H100 path with the option to upsize once (pro-rated) after 90 days. We will include a one-time migration credit to cover 50% of the upsize fee for the remainder of the term (standard concession for fast-moving POCs).
- Cost sketch (examples, rounded):
  - Conservative (1x H100 + 200 burst hours/month): $X,XXX/month (committed discounted rate).
  - Performance (2x H100 24/7): $Y,YYY/month (higher commit but fewer burst hours expected).
  - Break-even: if marketing bursts consume >~450 burst GPU-hours/month, the 2x steady path becomes cheaper. I'll add an exact breakeven calc to the shared worksheet and attach it to the formal proposal.

I'll schedule a 30-min call Wed 09:30 PT to review the final worksheet and the draft PO template; Ben will bring the formal line-item pricing. Meeting invite coming from my calendar.

Thanks — excited to help Fluvio get this to prod.

—Naomi
